title: Dede Westbrook's 232 Yards vs. Texas: OU Single-Game Record
question: Who holds Oklahoma's single-game receiving yards record?
answer: Dede Westbrook caught 10 passes for 232 yards and three touchdowns in Oklahoma's 45-40 win over Texas on Oct. 8, 2016, an Oklahoma single-game receiving record.
summary: Dede Westbrook's 10-catch, 232-yard, three-touchdown afternoon against Texas in 2016 set Oklahoma's single-game receiving yardage record in the Red River Showdown.
body: Oklahoma's single-game receiving yards record belongs to Dede Westbrook, and he set it on a big stage. On Oct. 8, 2016, the Sooners beat Texas 45-40 in Dallas, and Westbrook was at the center of it, finishing with 10 catches for 232 yards and three touchdowns.

His three scores covered 71, 42 and 47 yards, so almost all of his production came on explosive plays rather than short gains. Baker Mayfield threw for 390 yards in the game, and Westbrook was his favorite target all afternoon. Reports from CBS and Fox Sports both describe the 232 yards as an Oklahoma single-game receiving record.

The offense around him was just as busy. Oklahoma piled up 672 total yards, and Samaje Perine ran 35 times for 214 yards and two touchdowns. The teams combined for 85 points, which kept the Sooners from ever relaxing against a Texas team that kept answering.

The game fit into a remarkable season for Westbrook. He went on to win the Biletnikoff Award as the nation's top receiver and finished the year with 1,524 receiving yards and 17 touchdown catches. When fans ask who has the biggest receiving day in OU history, the answer is still that October afternoon in the Red River Showdown.
